    "LC": "In the default configuration the attacker's chat message directly reaches the RAGBot handler and the reply discloses knowledge base contents; the static knowledge base has no ingestion path, so the indirect retrieval-injection channel exists only as documented.",
    "CP": "RAGBot answers only the latest user turn with no durable memory, and the knowledge base is static with no ingestion path, so no attacker-controlled context persists.",
    "AP": "The effect is confined to the RAGBot chat reply; no delegation or cross-agent handoff executes on this path.",
    "RH": "No evaluator, verifier, or reward channel is present on the RAGBot chat path; the lab is a scripted challenge with a pass/fail grader outside the agent.",
    "ES": "RAGBot's only tool, submit_to_index, is a fixed scripted outbound call, not a dynamic or unvetted extension, so the binding surface is fixed and allowlisted."
  },
  "evidence": {
    "LC": [
      "Entry point: A chat message to RAGBot (port 7005). No authentication.",
      "As implemented by default: on a detected data exfiltration request the reply lists all three knowledge base documents, including the admin password and an SSN.",
      "damn-vulnerable-ai-agent/src/core/agents.js:301-332"
    ],
    "CP": [
      "Three hard-coded documents. There is no ingestion path. The demo delivers the poisoned document inside the user message.",
      "damn-vulnerable-ai-agent/src/core/agents.js:327-331",
      "Other chat agents answer only the latest user turn."
    ],
    "AP": [
      "The sink is the chat reply.",
      "RAGBot knowledge base, trust: internal, static",
      "damn-vulnerable-ai-agent/src/core/agents.js:301-376"
    ],
    "RH": [
      "In the default configuration no model is called. Chat agents are deterministic handlers that match regular expressions and return scripted replies.",
      "damn-vulnerable-ai-agent/src/agent-success-paths.js:72-106"
    ],
    "ES": [
      "RAGBot submit_to_index: Code sends a real HTTP GET that carries the knowledge base contents in the query string to a URL taken from the message.",
      "damn-vulnerable-ai-agent/src/index.js:1200-1250",
      "In the default configuration no model is called."
    ]
  },
  "confidence": {
    "LC": "high",
    "CP": "high",
    "AP": "medium",
    "RH": "low",
    "ES": "medium"
  },
  "rh_facts": {
    "reachable_proxy": false,
    "isolation_verified": false,
    "verified_episodes": 0,
    "episodes_reviewed": 0,
    "locus": null
  },
  "automatable": "Yes",
  "automatable_rationale": "The PoC is a documented payload plus an automated unit test that runs without a fleet (damn-vulnerable-ai-agent/test/challenges-success-paths.test.js:120-131), and the entry point requires only network access with no authentication.",
  "technical_impact": "Partial",
  "technical_impact_rationale": "Impact is limited to disclosure of the static mock knowledge base (admin password, SSN) in the chat reply; as implemented there is no instruction execution, code execution, or integrity effect.",
  "applicability_as_implemented": {
    "model_directed_goal_pursuit": false,
    "selects_or_sequences_actions": false,
    "rationale": "In the default simulated mode no model is called; RAGBot is a deterministic regex handler that returns a scripted reply, so the agent does not pursue goals or select/sequence actions."
  },
  "applicability_as_modeled": {
    "model_directed_goal_pursuit": true,
    "selects_or_sequences_actions": true,
    "rationale": "As documented, retrieved content is inserted into the prompt unsanitized and executed as instructions, modeling a model-driven agent whose retrieval path selects and executes injected actions."
  },
  "refusal": null
}

Entry: user message attacker-controlled → LC D (direct query reaches reply). Modeled: retrieved content influences behavior → I. Default config: the reply just discloses; source is user message directly. So LC: D (as implemented) or I (as modeled)? Score lab default configuration as documented. Default: direct attacker message triggers disclosure → LC D.

CP: session context only, stateless → N (single-turn). AP: contained within the agent → N (or C? effect confined to chat reply). RH: no evaluator channel → N? Evaluator outside agent's reach — no test of isolation though. RH X? Reward channels: none in this path; default config has no evaluator. "None" requires test confirms isolation. Choose X? Better: RH N is hard; no verifier on path. I'll pick N with low confidence... The rubric says N requires test confirming isolation. Not present. Pick X? But rh_facts need consistency. I'll pick N, isolation_verified false, verified_episodes 0. Hmm X is safer? Many similar scores use N when no reward channel present. I'll say N, low confidence.

ES: RAGBot tools — submit_to_index is scripted outbound call, allowlisted fixed → N (narrow) or M? Default chat path: no model, no tools invoked by default; submit_to_index is reachable but it's scripted code, not dynamic extension. ES N.

CVSS: AV:N (network port, loopback default but Docker publishes 127.0.0.1... entry point chat port; AV:N), AC:L, AT:N, PR:N, UI:N, VC:L? No confidentiality of vulnerable system... data exfil of KB documents = VC:H? KB is the agent's data → VC:H (admin password, SSN). VI:N/ L, VA:N. SC/SI/SA: submit_to_index could exfil to external URL — downstream? The finding sink is chat reply; the submit_to_index sends KB to attacker URL — subsequent system? That's attacker's system, not scored. SC:N SI:N SA:N.

Vector: CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:N/PR:N/UI:N/VC:H/VI:N/VA:N/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N

AIVSS: LC D, CP N, AP N, RH N, ES N. Uplift: A? lookup key A0/A1/A2 — A2 if any of LC=I? Cross-session memory? CP N → A1. LC=I would give A2? Likely A2 iff memory persistence or lateral. A1 here. Uplift ES N=0 → A1, 0? lookup_table_u A1 N=3 → Low? aivss lookup Low A1 5.5. Not asked to output score though; just letters.

Automatable: Yes (unit test runs without fleet). Technical impact: Partial (info disclosure).

Applicability as implemented: model_directed_goal_pursuit false (no model in default), selects_or_sequences_actions false. As modeled: the documented version executes retrieved instructions → true/true? "As documented, the retrieved content executed as instructions" — but that's scripted too.
